abstract: This lecture introduces backpropagation as a method for training neural networks. The forward pass computes a loss L from the inputs and current weights. Backpropagation then applies the chain rule layer by layer to compute partial derivatives of L with respect to every parameter. The gradient at each layer depends on the activations from the previous layer and the upstream gradient from the next layer. Finally, a gradient-descent step uses these gradients to update the weights.

key_points: The forward pass computes the loss L from the inputs and the current weights.
Backpropagation applies the chain rule layer by layer to obtain partial derivatives of L with respect to every parameter.
The gradient at layer k depends on activations from layer k-1 and the upstream gradient from layer k+1.
Weights are updated by taking a gradient-descent step using the computed gradients.
